newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government received promising indications that the economy may be lifting, as Moody's Investors Service yesterday announced the outlook for Australia's Aa2 credit rating was improving, and Australian Bureau of Statistics figures showed a sharp rise in retail sales, and a solid growth in housing approvals. Page 1.

As industry estimates claim A$2 billion may be lost a year in sales and uncollected taxes by Australian retailers and the Government to Internet trading, there are fears this figure could rise if proposals to establish a global free-trade zone on the Internet are adopted. There are hopes an inquiry by Parliament's Joint Committee of Public Accounts will come up with a way of collecting taxes on goods ordered overseas via the Internet. Page 1.

Just two days after the deregulation of Australia's telecommunications market, Telstra has submitted a plan for the charging of 013 directory assistance calls to the Federal Government. Telstra intends to charge 50 cents for 013 calls, and would give this money back to consumers by cutting A$5.40 a year off fixed-line rental charges. Page 3.

Former Australian Workers Union national secretary Vern Falconer, who only left the union this week after a brief stint, has told his colleagues that a "liquidation plan" must be devised to cover liabilities. Falconer has described the union's financial osition as "serious but retrievable". Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite the Reserve Bank of Australia's failure to deliver a widely anticipated interest rate cut yesterday, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said promising economic figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics coupled with a favourable budget assessment from United States ratings agency Moody's is leading the way to a "benign interest-rate climate". Page 1.

Communications Minister Richard Alston has supported Telstra's argument that the 100 million "non-genuine" calls made to the 013 directory assistance service would be reduced by charging 50 cents for 013 directory assistance calls and in turn reducing yearly phone rental charges. However, the issue has now been put to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Page 1.

The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said yesterday the pace of economic growth could be set back in 1997-98 as a result of the El Nino-driven pattern of widespread dry weather. ABARE estimated the effect could cost up to A$1.8 bilion in lost crop yields and production. Page 1.

Catholic officials in Australia were last night attempting to clarify an article published in Rome's Catholic University of the Sacred Heart's Medicine and Morality journal that stated physically and mentally disabled people should not engage in sex in case they produced similarly disabled children. Ethicists and disability groups have criticised the article, with Perth social worker Maija Tatis, who is affected by albinism, saying any suggestion that she should abstain from sex was an attack on her civil rights. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The independent Green Games Watch 2000 has this week revealed official documents showing that New South Wales Government agencies have known for nearly 20 years that drums of dioxin-contaminated waste are buried near where major Olympics venues, such as the athletes village, are being built. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said yesterday Australia's international credit rating could be upgraded by the end of the year after New York-based Moody's Investors Service announced Australia's credit standing was "improving". The announcement from Moody's is international recognition of the Federal Government's efforts to reduce the Budget deficit. Page 1.

New South Wales Transport Minister Brian Langton says the A$50 million control system for Sydney's rail system, which was launched in 1989 and designed to get the trains running on time, was a fiasco, after it was scrapped without ever being commissioned. Page 3.

The Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission awarded a record damages payout of A$55,000 to black French national Alex Rugema after racial abuse at his work, Melbourne-based company Southcorp Packaging caused him to suffer a severe depressive disorder. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a positive day for Australia's economy, debt ratings agency Moody's yesterday took the first step towards upgrading Australia's credit rating - a move that would lower interest payments on our A$250 billion foreign debt - and Bureau of Statistics figures showed strong results in the retail and housing sectors. Page 1.

Speaking in New York at the end of his two-week overseas trip, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday hinted tax reform would bring big tax cuts for low and middle-income earners, and also indicated the interest withholding tax system may be reformed, a mov that would ease relations with the international investment community. Page 1.

Victorian Returned Services League president Bruce Ruxton was re-elected yesterday for his 19th term, and came out attacking those responsible for pushing the debate on the republic, calling the Republic Advisory Committee "grant-funded bludgers". He als hit out at immigration, native title, Wik, homosexuals in the Defence Force, Governor-General Sir William Deane, and rural petrol prices. Page 1.

McDonald's Australia training and development director Rasfik Mankarious said yesterday the fast food chain will push to make its retail certificate part of the Victorian Certificate of Education curriculum. The scheme is believed to have been approved by the Department of Employment, Education, Training and Youth Affairs, and now only needs the support of the Board of Studies. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
